a disability-related modification or accommodation.

The Technology Task Force welcomes and encourages public participation at the Technology Task
Force meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to
comment or make a presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes or as specified by the
Chairperson. Anyone wishing to address the Technology Task Force is requested to fill out a
speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits the City to
identify persons for purposes of Technology Task Force minutes preparation.

Effective July 1, 2017, the Technology Task Force is responsible for developing a recommendation
to the City Council for the scope of an Advisory Committee on technology services serving the
community to be presented at the November 14, 2017 City Council meeting.

The Technology Task Force, at the direction of the Chairperson with concurrence of the Task

 Personal recommendation to technology task force

David Wagman, Chairperson

After a substantial amount of personal research, attending a presentation on wireless master plans by
the South Bay Council of Governments, and listening to the viewpoints of my fellow task force members
and the public at the first TTF meeting, I am of the opinion that there is work to be done of substantial
importance to PVE by a technology advisory committee. I am not yet clear on whether this work is of a
short term, ad hoc nature or whether there is a role for a standing committee.

There is an immediate need for the city to develop a Wireless Master Plan. This Plan should serve as a
guideline for how the city would prefer to see wireless construction and coverage unfold over time.
Although the city is limited in its control over cell siting, carriers would much prefer to go through a
simple process, which conforms to the city plan, rather than go their own route that might involve
fighting “city hall” every step of the way. We have an opportunity to direct the development of wireless
coverage as we would prefer (although clearly not in every case) if we act quickly to make our
preferences known to cell tower/antenna constructors. Absent a plan, we have little to no ability to
direct the proliferation of antennas and towers throughout our community.

As the City of PVE plans for the future, it would also be highly advisable for the city to have a crisp,
current understanding of the Fiber Optic Cable infrastructure deployed with city limits. This should
include active fiber, dark fiber and available conduit space inventories as well as ownership, tenancy,
origin, route and termination point information. Over time, it may be advisable for the city to own some
of this infrastructure, so knowing what is in place is vitally important.
Other technology projects, such as the South Bay Broadband Fiber Initiative, solar rooftop guidelines
and incentives, city preparation for self-driving automobile technology, and deployment of wi-fi
throughout the community could also be important areas of investigation for a technology advisory
committee.
 William Peckovich

  •  Develop and maintain a comprehensive inventory of telecommunications
  infrastructure in Palos Verdes Estates, including: copper infrastructure, fiber-
  optic infrastructure and wireless infrastructure.
  •  Interface with other area information and technology offices and committees,
  including: South Bay Cities Council of Governments, School District etc.
  •  Develop a communications master plan for the City designed to: simplify the
  process and direct infrastructure to benefit the City; minimize the visual
  impact of future wireless installations in the City; promote competition in the
  marketplace for all telecommunication services to residents of PVE.
  •  Review all applications for wireless cell sites and make recommendations to
  Planning Commission based upon communications master plan.
  •  Understand new legislation and make recommendations on working within
  guidelines to minimize impact on City aesthetically and financially.
   PVE TECH TASK FORCE
  Recommendations for the Task Force Committee
Author: Desiree Myers
Date: 9/7/17

I.  RECOMMENDED SCOPE ITEMS:

  1. Transparency of Public documents to the public; implement self-service and use of digital docs
  a. Benefit: Ease of use
  • Post on City Site
  • Use PDFs, not scanned docs: allowing search on words and phrases

  Require suppliers email documents, so they are already digitized

  •  Keep organized in an intuitive manner; facilitating ease of access
  •  Retain, minimally, the required duration by law – optimally longer
  •  Provides greater ease of use by Staff; facilitating efficiency
  b. Benefit: Reduces costs SIGNIFICANTLY:
  • Reduce/eliminate record requests costs paid by residents
  • Reduce/eliminate city cost of records request because most/all requests are
  then facilitated by self help
  • Reduces/eliminates costs for copy machines, maintenance, paper, ink
  cartridges, shredding, filing cabinets, filling efforts, retrieval efforts, duplication,
  faxing, scanning, offsite storage and transportation, etc.

  c. Benefit: Reduces the opportunity for Fraud
  Reduces/eliminates fraud and the perception of wrong doing: inherent in full
  transparency is the elimination of opportunity to commit fraud. This is why the state of
  California created the CPRA laws.

  d. Benefit: Is a Green

  Reduces PVE’s carbon footprint; as recommended by the City Mgr in his
  recommendation and passage of PVE’s “Climate Agenda”. Eliminates most paper,
  transport to offsite storage, duplication and shredding.

  e. Benefit: Prepares for a disaster

  Simply create a copy of the master digital copy and store offsite and, in case a disaster,
  you will be ready to start up anywhere. This can be fully automated.

  f.  Align to best practices:
   • National
  Standards: https://www.nationaltransparencyassociation.com/transparency-
  awards/
  • Is better prepared for CA law changes which currently seek better access; so the
  City can discontinue writing letters to CA Assembly that takes a stand against
  public access to public documents; sending the wrong message to residents

  g. Builds Community trust:
  •  Community trust is challenged by the City, engaging in 7 years of deficit
  spending; leaving residents concerned about where all the money is going. To
  build trust, engage in activities that show the City has nothing to hide and is
  receptive of resident concerns.
  •  RPV has self-serve for documents on their site, including all their contracts. Why
  should PVE have lower transparency standards?
  •  MCHA has requested common public information (far less than National
  Standards above) be available on PVE’S site, yet, the City declined to make most
  information available. This sends a message.

  Cost effective approach:

  I will help you for free. This self-service solution can be implemented in 2 weeks, with
  minimal time and cost; mostly just procedural changes, space provided on the server
  that is shown on the PVE site.

2. Obtain required Skills for Management of the Financial systems to download expenses

  PVE uses Pentamation for their Accounts Payable software. Pentamation if fully capable for
  creating a download of the checks that have been written. This will allow PVE to reach level 2 of
  the standard business practices of City
  Transparency: https://www.nationaltransparencyassociation.com/transparency-awards/
  This information allows review of expenses, a standard business practice to reduce costs. And,
  it ensures proper oversight of expenditures. The City Mgr has inhouse and contracted
  Accounting staff, but has said he does any skills to download expenses. The contract for the
  Accountant needs to be changed to utilize someone with the necessary skills on Pentamation.
  Reviewing expenses and reducing waste is essential for the City to show they have done their
  part to address the Financial problems; restoring trust in the community that the City is
  effectively managing the people’s resources.

3. Get a competitor in PVE to COX

  People seek better pricing and increase in reliability of services, that other cities receive

4. Ensure Supplier Contracts with the City – benefit & protect residents

  This includes protection of resident private information, competitive pricing, reliability of
  services with service level agreements with consequences. This includes implementing the
   standard business practice of signing off on receipt of services and products upon receipt; and
  prohibiting supplier invoicing without inclusion of city signoffs of receipt.

  5. Protect Resident Personal Information

  Review all City Contracts to ensure proper protection of the resident’s personal information; i.e.
  that this data is not captured and share in a supplier’s database, in the course of any of their
  services. And if it is, the Council is to be notified and modifications put in place to protect the
  residents.

  Standards should be pre-established one how to handle this situation:

  •  What needs to go into contracts
  •  Any follow-up/audit that should take place

II.  RECOMMENDED GUIDING PRINCIPALS:

  •  The Tech Committee serves the residents and the resident interests.
  •  The Tech Committee listens to the residents and advises based on the residents needs and
  desires.
  •  The Tech Committee actively engages residents; utilizing their input & feedback
  •  Tech Committee addresses internal and external issues in relation to the needs and priorities of
  the community.
  •  Staff serves to the needs of the public; providing information and support needed by the Tech
  Committee in their service to the public
  •  The Tech Committee should be a body of diverse opinions, expertise and perspectives;
  replicating the community and community needs.

III.  RECOMMENDED APPROACH:

  •  Tech Committee and Tech Task Force agendas should be inclusive of diverse opinions; therefore
  should include “members’ reports”, like Council meetings

  •  The City should let the community know of the Tech Task Force; ensuring community
  opportunity for input and feedback.

  •  Evolution of the Tech Committee’s scope should be anticipated and therefore planned by the
  Tech Task force. So, define how this is allow to change. For instance, perhaps:

  a. The Tech Committee submits scope changes to the Council; added to Council agenda:
  o - the scope (or project) name
   o - a concise description of the problem/opportunity/need from the city perspective
  o - the tech committee proposed role (inputs, work that will be done, outputs)
  b. Conversely, perhaps the Council would like to add scope or a project for the Tech
  Committee; so, establish how is this done.

•  Establish a means that the Tech Committee can utilize sub-committees readily for hands-on
  efforts:
  o For instance, a Cell Tower sub-committee and/or an IT Sub-Committee
  o How can/should other residents who have expertise be included?

  Encourage Tech Committee members to freely engage outside help to do their job. Not
  to the extent of committing city resources, but the Tech Committee should be
  encouraged to get support from outside experts (residents preferred, but not required)
  accomplish its objectives.
